takeaway: GPHash makes persistent-memory indexing GPU-native through warp-cooperative bucket probes, atomic slot-state updates, and a periodically frozen hot-bucket cache.
background: Byte-addressable persistent memory mapped into a GPU address space can hold durable data beyond GPU-memory capacity without CPU-mediated transfers. Hash indexing suits point access, but conventional CPU and GPU tables do not account for warp execution, persistence, or the large PM-to-GPU bandwidth gap.
villain: One-operation-per-thread tables suffer warp divergence and uncoalesced reads, locks contend across thousands of threads, and logging or copy-on-write adds persistent writes. Directly probing PM also leaves GPU compute starved by comparatively low media bandwidth.
approach: GPHash assigns one operation to a 32-thread warp, which probes all candidate slots together in coalesced accesses. Multi-level shared buckets, multiple hash locations, and associativity raise load factor. CAS plus empty/insertion slot states provides lock- and log-free failure atomicity. BktCache periodically loads hot whole buckets into GPU memory and freezes membership between refreshes.
impact: The design shows how data-structure layout, concurrency, durability, and caching must all follow GPU execution granularity when accelerators directly manage persistent data. Its configurable structure trades lookup throughput against load factor.

evaluation.overview: YCSB point operations and mixes measure throughput, latency, load factor, design contributions, sensitivity, recovery, and resize/cache-load overhead; DLRM and PageRank traces test application-derived access.
evaluation.implemented: An open-source CUDA hash index for GPU-mapped persistent memory with warp-cooperative operations and a GPU-resident bucket cache.
evaluation.setting: A dual-26-core Xeon Gold 6230R server with a Tesla V100, 192 GB DRAM, and six Optane DCPMMs totaling 768 GB in App Direct mode; indexes begin with 16 million items.

results.text: Across YCSB operations, GPHash is reported to improve throughput by up to 13.84× and reduce latency by up to 27.62× versus CPU-assisted indexes; insertion throughput improves by up to 5.79×.
GPHash reaches a maximum 92% load factor versus at most 85% for the compared persistent-memory tables and 82% for SlabHash-GPM.
On DLRM- and PageRank-derived workloads, GPHash reports up to 7.09× higher throughput and 7.91× lower latency than the comparison schemes.

limitations: The prototype uses one V100 and deprecated Optane PM rather than a CXL-attached system, although the authors argue the design transfers. It optimizes point access, not range queries, and variable-length records depend on a suitable GPU allocator. Results use batched operations and mostly fixed-size keys/values; BktCache benefits depend on skew and consumes GPU memory.
phd_group_signal: The paper treats GPU warp behavior and PM persistence as first-class data-structure constraints, then decomposes gains among execution, layout, and caching. It demonstrates the accelerator-systems practice of redesigning rather than mechanically porting a CPU structure.

claims.text: One warp probes all slots in candidate buckets, while associativity, inter-level sharing, multiple hash locations, and in-place keys combine high parallelism with coalesced access.
Atomic CAS transitions through reserved slot states make insertion, update, and deletion lock-free and recoverable without a separate log.
